options.explanation: p ∝ T at fixed volume — the ratio carries both ways.
The temperature rose, not fell.

questions.stem: State the pressure law in words.
questions.modelAnswer: With the sample sealed in a rigid container, the pressure is directly proportional to the kelvin temperature.

questions.stem: State the conversion that must be applied to temperatures before using the pressure law.
questions.modelAnswer: Celsius temperatures must be converted to kelvin by adding 273 before substituting into the law.

questions.stem: Explain why the pressure–kelvin temperature graph of a fixed gas at constant volume is a straight line through the origin.
questions.modelAnswer: Pressure is proportional to kelvin temperature: at 0 K the molecules would have minimum energy, deliver no wall collisions, and produce no pressure. A proportional relationship plotted from its true zero is a straight line through the origin, which is exactly what the extrapolated measurements show for every gas.

questions.stem: A bicycle tyre holds air at a pressure of 5.10 × 10^5 Pa with the temperature at 279 K. Once ridden, the air warms to 299 K while the volume stays fixed. Calculate the new pressure.
questions.modelAnswer: p2 = p1 × T2/T1 = 5.10 × 10^5 × 299/279 = 5.47 × 10^5 Pa (3 s.f.). The warmer tyre holds proportionally higher pressure.
